title: Bond Yields Spike: What Happens To Your Wallet Next? | Steve Hanke
speaker: Steve Hanke

macro_themes.view: Divisia M4 growing 7.4%, above his 6% 'golden' rate, so inflation (CPI 3.4% y/y, 5.1% 6-month annualised) will not return to 2%; inflation is out of the bottle.
Fed will keep raising rates while labor market holds, but hot AI credit demand keeps money supply accelerating.
Six drivers (money growth, AI credit demand, tariffs/ad hoc policy, Iran war, China policy, weak confidence) keep yields elevated; risk of a bond buyer strike.
No recession signs yet as money supply accelerates, but outside AI investment is falling; an AI bust would be a real problem.
Unaffordable for buyers, which supports investing in rental property.

calls.reason: Would stay away from nominal bonds because of accelerating money supply, AI credit demand, tariffs, Iran war and weak confidence; only TIPS are attractive.
calls.quote: I I'd stay away from these nominal bonds... the nominals. I I I wouldn't get into them.

calls.reason: Secular gold bull intact despite rising yields; sees the eventual market top at $6,000-7,000.
calls.quote: the secular bull is intact and and it'll continue to go up... the top of the market will be like $6,000 $7,000 an ounce

notes: Host states Tuesday, September 29th. Gold target given as a range $6,000-7,000 (recorded 6000). TLT used for his avoid-nominal-bonds view; he implies yields stay high but gives no explicit yield target.
